detail.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes an out-of-bounds write in `QuantizedDBuffer.quantize_` (MFSDP v2, MXFP8; TE side issue: NVIDIA/TransformerEngine#3689).

**Symptom.** Using MFSDP v2 + MXFP8 `fully_shard` initialization can cause `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` from TE's `quantize_mxfp8` kernel (`FsdpParameterGroup.sync_model_weight_from_main_weight` -> `QuantizedDBuffer.quantize_`). Some devices ran with silently corrupted neighbouring scales.

**Root cause.** TE's MXFP8 quantize kernel assumes `scale_inv` has the padded physical shape from `get_scale_shape()` and stores a scale for every row of its 64-row chunk, including rows beyond the tensor (NVIDIA/TransformerEngine#3689). `quantize_` passed it the compact per-parameter scale views of the local planes, so whenever a rank's shard is not a multiple of 64 rows (32 rows per rank for the output layer at DP 128) the kernel wrote beyond the view: into the next rank's chunk of the replicated plane, or beyond the end of the local buffer. This is the producer-side counterpart of NVIDIA/TransformerEngine#3518, which `get_tensor()` already works around for GEMM; that issue's 64x64 example stays in bounds, which is why `quantize_` appeared to accept compact scales.

**Fix.** Quantize into the padded scale tensors that `get_tensor()` already builds for the GEMM path and copy the compact region back into the plane views. Data planes are exact and stay views. The extra allocation and copy happen only for parameters whose local shard needs padding and are freed on return; they go away once TE handles compact scales on both paths.

**Test.** `test_quantized_dbuffer_quantize_writes_only_the_local_shard`: a replicated `QuantizedDBuffer` filled with a canary, viewed as `BlockAtomic(32)` (what `FsdpParameterGroup` does) and quantized; asserts the other ranks' chunks of every plane are untouched and the local shard matches TE's reference quantizer. Fails on every rank before this change (`rowwise_scale chunk of rank N+1 was written`), passes after. The existing `test_quantized_dbuffer_quantization_matches_te` cannot catch this because in-order quantization overwrites the corrupted neighbour and the last tensor's out-of-bounds write lands in allocator slack.

detail.title: Pad the scale buffers before calling TE's quantize

files.patch:
@@ -228,7 +228,28 @@ def quantize_(self, main_weight: DBuffer) -> None:
             if actual != expected:
                 raise ValueError(f"Expected main_weight {attribute} {expected!r}, got {actual!r}.")
         for index in range(len(self.rowwise_data.layout.tensor_shapes)):
-            self.get_tensor_view(index).quantize_(main_weight.get_tensor_view(index))
+            # TE's MXFP8 quantize kernel writes scale_inv in its padded physical
+            # layout (see _pad_rowwise_scale and _pad_columnwise_scale) and stores
+            # scales for every row of its 64-row chunk, including rows beyond the
+            # tensor (https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/issues/3689). The
+            # compact plane views are smaller than that whenever this rank's shard
+            # is not a multiple of 64 rows, so quantizing into them is an
+            # out-of-bounds write: into the next rank's chunk of a replicated plane,
+            # or beyond the end of the local buffer. This is the producer-side
+            # counterpart of the GEMM padding in get_tensor() (TE issue 3518):
+            # quantize into the padded scales that get_tensor() builds and copy the
+            # compact region back. Once TE quantizes into compact scales in bounds,
+            # this loop body reduces to:
+            #   self.get_tensor_view(index).quantize_(main_weight.get_tensor_view(index))
+            tensor = self.get_tensor(index)
+            tensor.quantize_(main_weight.get_tensor_view(index))
+            for plane, padded in (
+                (self.rowwise_scale, tensor._rowwise_scale_inv),
+                (self.columnwise_scale, tensor._columnwise_scale_inv),
+            ):
+                compact = plane.get_tensor_view(index)
+                if padded.shape != compact.shape:
+                    compact.copy_(padded[: compact.shape[0], : compact.shape[1]])
 
     @property
     def planes(self) -> tuple[DBuffer, DBuffer, DBuffer, DBuffer]:

@@ -29,15 +29,45 @@
     pytest.skip("MXFP8 quantization is not available.", allow_module_level=True)
 
 
-def test_quantized_dbuffer_quantization_matches_te(distributed_setup):
-    """Quantized tensor views match TE's data and scales."""
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "placements",
+    [
+        pytest.param((BlockAtomic(32),), id="shard"),
+        pytest.param((Replicate(), BlockAtomic(32)), id="replicate_shard"),
+        pytest.param((BlockAtomic(32), BlockAtomic(32)), id="shard_shard"),
+    ],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "make_shapes",
+    [
+        pytest.param(lambda num_ranks: [(128, 128), (128, 128), (64, 64), (32, 64)], id="mixed"),
+        # One 32-row tensor per layout chunk, so every shard ends with a 32-row tensor.
+        # TE's quantize kernel writes scales for whole 64-row chunks, so compact scale
+        # views would be written beyond: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/issues/3689
+        pytest.param(lambda num_ranks: [(32, 128)] * num_ranks, id="short_tensors"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_quantized_dbuffer_quantization_matches_te(distributed_setup, placements, make_shapes):
+    """Quantizing a sharded view matches TE and writes only this rank's shard.
+
+    The view is taken from a replicated buffer filled with a canary, so any write
+    outside this rank's shard lands in memory the test owns and is detected.
+    """
     device = distributed_setup.device
-    mesh = init_device_mesh(device.type, (distributed_setup.world_size,))
-    shapes = [(128, 128), (128, 128), (64, 64), (32, 64)]
-    quantized = QuantizedDBuffer.empty(mesh, [BlockAtomic(32)], shapes, device)
-    main_weight = DBuffer(
-        mesh, [BlockAtomic(32)], quantized.rowwise_data.layout, torch.float32, device
-    )
+    world_size = distributed_setup.world_size
+    if len(placements) == 1:
+        mesh = init_device_mesh(device.type, (world_size,))
+    else:
+        if world_size < 4 or world_size % 2:
+            pytest.skip("Two-dimensional placements require an even world size of at least 4.")
+        mesh = init_device_mesh(device.type, (2, world_size // 2))
+    shapes = make_shapes(mesh.size())
+    canary = 0xAA
+    replicated = QuantizedDBuffer.empty(mesh, [Replicate()] * mesh.ndim, shapes, device)
+    for plane in replicated.planes:
+        plane.local_buffer.fill_(canary)
+    quantized = replicated.view(placements)
+    main_weight = DBuffer(mesh, placements, quantized.rowwise_data.layout, torch.float32, device)
     torch.manual_seed(1234 + distributed_setup.rank)
     main_weight.local_buffer.normal_()
     quantized.quantize_(main_weight)
@@ -63,6 +93,11 @@ def test_quantized_dbuffer_quantization_matches_te(distributed_setup):
                 actual, expected[: actual.shape[0], : actual.shape[1]], rtol=0, atol=0
             )
 
+    # Restore the canary in this rank's shard; anything else that changed was written outside it.
+    for plane in quantized.planes:
+        plane.local_buffer.fill_(canary)
+    assert all(plane.local_buffer.eq(canary).all() for plane in replicated.planes)
+
 
 def test_quantized_dbuffer_get_tensor_supports_gemm(distributed_setup):
     """Compute tensors prepare gathered scales for rowwise and columnwise GEMMs."""

inline_comments.body: Can you keep this code in code comment? This way, when this TE bug is fixed, we know what the right Megatron code should be.
Nit: can test_quantized_dbuffer_quantization_matches_te be changed/extended to cover this so we don't need yet another similar test?
Yes. We now  parametrize `test_quantized_dbuffer_quantization_matches_te` over the distinct placements and shapes, and assert no out-of-bound write.
